The perimeter fence is incomplete. A portion of the perimeter fence also serves as the rear wall of the enclosure housing
three kangaroos and three wallabies, leaving that portion of the enclosure without a separate perimeter fence.
Failure to provide a complete perimeter fence may allow unwanted animals or unauthorized persons to gain access to or
have contact with the animals.
Outdoor housing facilities must be enclosed by a perimeter fence that is at least three feet from the primary enclosure and
serves as a secondary containment system. To be corrected by October 22, 2026.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with a facility representative.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:
